issues.description: Resource IDs are interpolated into URL paths without percent-encoding, allowing slash/query/path injection into API routes.
batch_create materializes the entire iterable before chunking, contradicting the any-size iterable API and risking large memory spikes.
batch_create silently drops malformed or missing result entries instead of validating result count, index uniqueness, and item shape.
Pagination silently ignores non-mapping items, causing possible data loss instead of surfacing malformed API responses.
Pagination has no guard against repeated cursors, so a bad API response can create an infinite request loop.
Retry-After handling accepts only numeric seconds, ignores HTTP-date values, and has no maximum sleep cap.
Transport errors and timeouts are not wrapped in LumenAPIError, leaking raw httpx exceptions through the public client API.
max_attempts is not validated, so zero or negative values skip the request and produce a misleading generic error.
Runtime parsing accepts invalid Literal values for status, state, batch status, and review verdict instead of rejecting bad API data.
Error.from_dict coerces retryable with bool(), so string values like "false" become True.
Model parsers coerce null or wrong-typed scalar fields with str/int/float, which can corrupt malformed API data instead of failing fast.
review always sends note:null when note is omitted, which can differ from omitting the field for APIs that distinguish absent and null.
Package advertises a typed client but does not include a PEP 561 py.typed marker, so downstream type checkers may not consume its inline types.
Tests cover happy-path pagination/retries/batching but miss malformed responses, path escaping, transport failures, enum validation, and annotation listing.
